articles.title: Energy-Saving System for Marine Generators Touts 10% Fuel Savings
articles.summary: NYK Line, MTI Co., Oshima Shipbuilding, Terasaki Electric and Daihatsu Infinearth have verified the energy-saving performance and operational safety of the Hz Controller System, an energy-saving system for marine generators developed through joint testing.
articles.body: Energy-Saving System for Marine Generators Touts 10% Fuel Savings Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 20, 2026 Copyright Xavier MARCHANT/AdobeStock NYK Line, MTI Co., Oshima Shipbuilding, Terasaki Electric and Daihatsu Infinearth have verified the energy-saving performance and operational safety of the Hz Controller System, an energy-saving system for marine generators developed through joint testing. General sales of the system will now begin. Building on their joint research, the five companies will expand deployment beyond NYK-operated vessels, promoting installation on newbuildings and retrofitting on existing ships owned by other shipowners. The System reduces power consumption and generator fuel consumption by lowering the generator frequency while maintaining the performance required by onboard equipment. This is possible because onboard equipment such as pumps and motors that operate in conjunction with the power supply frequency is designed to deliver the required performance even under anticipated severe conditions and may therefore have excess capacity during normal navigation. Specifically, the System switches between the regular frequency and a lower energy-saving frequency according to shipboard conditions within the range specified by ship classification rules. It utilizes generator frequency control technology (Patent Number JP6238600) that is jointly patented by NYK and Tsuneishi Shipbuilding. Demonstration tests confirmed an approximately 10% reduction in generator fuel consumption compared with operation at the regular frequency. Subsequent verification on an increasing number of vessels equipped with the system confirmed a similar reduction. For general sales, Terasaki Electric will be responsible for the design and supply of the System, while Daihatsu Infinearth will expand its lineup of generator engines compatible with the System.

articles.title: 1 MW floating wave energy converter gets green light for test site deployment
articles.summary: WEDUSEA, a €19.6 million collaborative project bringing together 14 European partners, has secured a marine license that allows the installation...
articles.body: Tidal & Wave Energy November 20, 2026 · 1 minute ago 1 MW floating wave energy converter gets green light for test site deployment NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email EMEC WEDUSEA, a €19.6 million collaborative project bringing together 14 European partners, has secured a marine license that allows the installation of a 1 MW OE Buoy floating wave energy converter and associated moorings at the European Marine Energy Centre's (EMEC) test site in Orkney. Co-funded by the EU Horizon Europe Programme and Innovate UK, WEDUSEA, which brings together 14 partners from industry and academia across Ireland, the UK, France, Germany and Spain, aims to create a step change for the wave energy industry and support its progression towards commercialization. The marine license granted by the Marine Directorate, previously Marine Scotland, allows the 1 MW-rated, unmanned floating oscillating water column device, developed by OceanEnergy, to be deployed at EMEC. Its only moving part, the turbine rotor, sits on deck above the waves, while all electrical equipment is housed below deck in a sealed machine room. As waves cause air trapped within the OE Buoy hull to oscillate, the airflow drives the turbine to generate electricity. This electricity will be exported to the grid via an underwater umbilical and export cable, EMEC explained. The OE Buoy and its mooring system will be installed at Berth 5 at the Billia Croo wave energy test site. Furthermore, EMEC has developed an extensive environmental monitoring plan for the deployment, which will monitor the habitat above and below the water’s surface in the vicinity of the OE Buoy. The monitoring program will begin before installation to establish a baseline of benthic and pelagic activity in the deployment area, helping to build understanding of the marine environment before, during and following deployment. articles.body: US Coast Guard Commissions New Cutter for Caribbean Ops Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 20, 2026 (Credit: US Coast Guard) The U.S. Coast Guard has commissioned its newest Sentinel-class fast response cutter, USCGC Marvin Perrett (WPC 1164), during a ceremony in New Orleans, ahead of the vessel's deployment to its homeport in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The commissioning ceremony took place at the Julia Street Cruise Ship Terminal, marking the cutter's official entry into active service. Following commissioning, the vessel and its crew will transit to San Juan, from where they will conduct operations across the Caribbean and the United States' southern maritime approaches. Its missions will include search and rescue, maritime law enforcement and homeland security operations. The Sentinel-class cutter is equipped with advanced maritime sensors, integrated intelligence and communications systems, and capabilities for deploying pursuit boats over the horizon. The Coast Guard said the vessel would strengthen its capacity to conduct maritime security, border protection and search and rescue missions in the region. The cutter is named after Marvin Perrett, a New Orleans native and Coast Guard veteran who operated Higgins landing craft during World War II, participating in the Normandy landings and subsequent operations in southern France and the Pacific. Perrett later received a Knight of the Legion of Honor medal from France in recognition of his wartime service.

articles.body: Cabling November 20, 2026 · 1 minute ago Nexans completes deep-water cable laying ops off Australia for Chevron NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Nexans Nexans has completed the laying and trenching of the high-voltage dynamic cable for Chevron's Jansz-Io Compression (J-IC) project offshore Western Australia. The cable-laying vessel (CLV) Nexans Aurora installed 26 buoyancy modules and trenched 30 kilometers of cable, after which it left Australia on October 23. J-IC uses subsea compression to sustain gas supply to the Gorgon LNG and domestic gas plants on Barrow Island. The 145 kV cable, about 135 kilometers long, runs from the island to a floating field control station, which powers and controls the compressors on the seabed. The completed operation included the overboarding and pull-in of the cable head to the field control station, installation of the buoyancy modules using a horizontal method developed, laying of the cable in its dynamic configuration, installation of about 200 meters of vortex-induced vibration (VIV) strakes in the Scarp section, cable lay up the Scarp, float-out and pull-in of the second cable end at Barrow Island, as-laid survey and cable trenching. Before handover, the remaining work includes cable jointing at the field control station and on Barrow Island, rock stabilization along the last 28 kilometers of the route, and final soak test, planned for February. Nexans Chevron sanctioned the Jansz-Io compression project in early July 2021 and ordered the field control station from the Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering (DSME) shipyard, now known as Hanwha Ocean, a few months later.
